title: Milestone 2026.04.91 - Operational Efficiency Retrospective
source_notes: Uses the provided milestone timing data as authoritative: 495 minutes, 113 completed experiments, reported average approximately 4 minutes per experiment.
The arithmetic average is 495 / 113 = 4.38 minutes per experiment; the provided '4 minutes' figure is treated as rounded operational shorthand.
ops/changelog.md records the active .91 experiment range as exp1165-exp1177 and the research milestone result as 11 of 13 criteria met.

results/experiment_1177_milestone_retro_91.json is research-focused and records two missed criteria: paper_v4_phase4_section_integrated=false and grpo_v5_honest_result=false. This artifact focuses on execution efficiency rather than research merit.

GPU close state was provided as a gpu_monitor.py report at 2026-05-02T22:01:53.785811+00:00: both RTX 3090s idle, 4 MB allocated each, 0% utilization, no process list, and three underutilization suggestions.

slowest_experiments.title: Code Repair 50q Scale-Up - IterativeSelfRepair with Gemma4
slowest_experiments.why_slow: Recurring full-queue carryover benchmark. The underlying workload is inherently expensive because it runs sequential execute-feedback-retry loops across 50 code-repair questions with a large model, but the operational problem is that this retired/carryover item still reaches dispatch. A dispatch-time retirement guard would remove the entire 35-minute recurrence.

slowest_experiments.title: In-process docs for Exp 950: E-MVL Sparsified Ising - Sparse Connectivity for KV260 RTL Optimization
slowest_experiments.why_slow: Inline documentation reconciliation blocked the executor. This pass has no dependency that requires occupying the experiment execution lane; it should be batched as an asynchronous milestone-close reconciliation task.

slowest_experiments.title: Symbolic-KAN Real FoVer Data - AUC=0.9344 Architecture
slowest_experiments.why_slow: CPU-bound full-corpus FoVer architecture sweep. For exploratory/non-certification comparisons, the run should use a bounded fast-eval sample and reserve full-corpus sweeps for final certification artifacts.

slowest_experiments.title: Math Iterative Self-Repair v1 - Execute-Feedback on GSM8K
slowest_experiments.why_slow: Sequential repair loop with per-question feedback and limited batching. Stable benchmark fixtures should cache unchanged baseline outputs, batch model calls, and rerun only components changed by the current milestone.

slowest_experiments.title: IterativeSelfRepair v1 - Execute-Feedback-Retry on HumanEval
slowest_experiments.why_slow: Same fixture pattern as exp930: repeated serial execute-feedback-retry work where cached outputs, early-stop rules, and batched GPU execution would reduce wall time without changing the benchmark's purpose.

bottlenecks_identified: Frozen slowest-five composition persisted into .91: exp906, exp950 docs, exp948, exp930, and exp905 remain the top wall-time consumers. The milestone improved overall wall time, but the improvement was mostly volume-driven rather than evidence that these bottlenecks were fixed.
Dispatch-time retirement/carryover enforcement is still incomplete. exp906 consumed 35 minutes again despite being a recurring retired/carryover slow-path item from prior retros.
Documentation reconciliation is still inline. The 28-minute exp950 docs pass directly blocked the execution queue and is the clearest non-research bottleneck.
Full-corpus CPU sweeps are still used for exploratory work. exp948 consumed 24 minutes where a fast-eval sample would likely have been sufficient until final certification.
Benchmark fixtures are still rerun serially. exp930 and exp905 consumed 36 combined minutes and should use cached baselines, delta evaluation, batching, and early-stop rules.

GPU utilization was inefficient at milestone close. Both RTX 3090s were idle at 0% utilization with only 4 MB allocated each. The gpu_monitor.py suggestions explicitly recommended DualGPURunner with Qwen on GPU 0 and Gemma on GPU 1.

No GPU zombie processes were detected from the provided monitor report. The 4 MB allocations are below gpu_monitor.py's zombie threshold of at least 1024 MB for more than 10 idle minutes and look like driver residual allocations rather than resource leaks.

GRPO v5 exposed a GPU-offload infrastructure gap rather than a research bottleneck: exp1173 hit the training wall with dualgpu_confirmed=false because the llama.cpp runtime lacked GPU offload support. That should be caught before dispatch for DualGPU-mandatory work.

Pre-flight testing was not the primary .91 bottleneck. No pre-flight suite item appears in the slowest-five timing list. The remaining gate/runtime failures were more specific: publication figure/hardware-claim audit readiness and llama.cpp GPU-offload availability.

Several .91 experiments were independent after exp1168/exp1169 and could have run concurrently with doc reconciliation or stable benchmark fixture reruns. GPU-eligible model work should also default to dual-GPU parallel execution instead of occupying one sequential lane.

questions_answered.which_experiments_took_longest_and_why: The slowest five were exp906 at 35 minutes, exp950 in-process docs at 28 minutes, exp948 at 24 minutes, exp930 at 19 minutes, and exp905 at 17 minutes. The reasons were recurring dispatch of retired/carryover benchmarks, inline doc reconciliation, full-corpus CPU sweeps, and serial repair fixture execution.
questions_answered.was_gpu_utilization_efficient: No. Both RTX 3090s were idle at close: 4/24576 MB on each GPU, 0% utilization, 53-54C. The monitor recommended DualGPURunner for simultaneous Qwen/Gemma execution.
questions_answered.were_there_zombie_processes: No zombies were evident in the provided report. gpu_monitor.py defines zombies as processes using at least 1024 MB VRAM, idle for more than 10 minutes, with CPU/wall ratio below 1%. The report only showed 4 MB allocated per GPU and no process list.
questions_answered.could_any_experiments_have_been_parallel: Yes. Inline docs could run asynchronously, exp905/exp930 benchmark fixtures could run in parallel with CPU doc/spec work, and GPU-eligible model jobs should default to DualGPURunner. Independent Phase 2/3 tasks after the SC-Energy/FoVer gate could also run in separate lanes.
questions_answered.was_the_preflight_test_suite_a_bottlenec: Not materially in .91. It was not in the slowest-five list. The dominant pre-dispatch issues were absent runtime capabilities and publication-audit readiness, not a large pre-flight test-suite wall.
questions_answered.were_doc_reconciliation_passes_efficient: No. exp950's 28-minute in-process doc pass was the second-slowest item and should be an asynchronous milestone-close batch.
questions_answered.what_tooling_infrastructure_changes_woul: Prioritize dispatch-time retirement guard, async doc reconciliation, CARNOT_FAST_EVAL for exploratory sweeps, cached/delta benchmark fixture evaluation, DualGPURunner as the default GPU policy, and a pre-dispatch GPU-offload probe for llama.cpp/DualGPU-mandatory experiments.

improvements_suggested: Add a dispatch-time retirement guard that checks the exclusion manifest immediately before worker spawn and emits a skipped/blocked artifact without launching the experiment. Include exp906 as a regression test case.

Move doc reconciliation out of the main experiment lane. Batch ops/spec/changelog/docs reconciliation as a single asynchronous milestone-close task and fail the milestone only on reconciliation errors, not while blocking active experiments.
Implement CARNOT_FAST_EVAL=1 for exploratory FoVer/Symbolic-KAN sweeps. Default to a bounded 500-pair or stratified sample unless the task is explicitly marked certification/full-corpus.
Cache stable benchmark fixture outputs for exp905/exp930-style repair loops. Recompute only changed repair/verifier logic and batch model calls across questions where possible.
Make DualGPURunner the default for requires_gpu experiments. Assign Qwen-class and Gemma-class workloads to separate RTX 3090s unless a task opts out with a reason.
Add a pre-dispatch GPU-offload capability probe for llama.cpp and other local inference backends. DualGPU-mandatory experiments should not launch until GPU offload is verified.
Split milestone execution lanes into CPU-doc, CPU-eval, GPU-model, and gated-publication queues. This would let doc reconciliation and stable CPU sweeps proceed without holding GPU-critical work.

Make the pre-flight suite report both duration and blocking reason per check. .91 was not pre-flight-bound, but richer timing would prevent future bottleneck attribution from relying on operator inference.

Record per-experiment start/end timestamps and GPU occupancy in ops/metrics.md automatically so operational retros do not need to infer efficiency from slowest-five excerpts and close-state snapshots.

estimated_savings_breakdown_min.note: The headline estimate is conservative because some savings overlap when queues run in parallel.

wall_time_trend.trend_note: 495 minutes is another project-best wall time, but the slowest-five freeze shows the system is still carrying avoidable recurring overhead.
